title: The best of people
hookLine: the best of people are those most useful to people (Tabarani)
tomorrow: a new city, his first words to it. what were they?

lines: CALL ME IF YOU NEED ANYTHING.
cards: After a funeral, a house fills with people who don't know what to do with their hands. Someone straightens chairs. Someone says, call me if you need anything, and means it, and nobody ever calls.

And then there's the one who shows up on Tuesday with a pot of rice and a roll of trash bags, and quietly takes out the recycling. When news came that his cousin Ja'far had died, the Prophet ﷺ didn't give a speech.
He gave an instruction about dinner.

teach.b: Make food for Ja'far's family, he said, in Abu Dawud's collection, for something has come upon them that keeps them busy. Not a sermon. Food.

That's the door into a new stretch of this path, service, and its first line is a hadith in al-Tabarani's collection: the best of people are those most useful to people. Notice the word people, both times.
Not only Muslims, not only family.

teach.h: NATIONS AND TRIBES, TO KNOW ONE ANOTHER.
teach.b: The Qur'an says it just as wide: "O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct."
One human family, measured by how it acts.
Now look back at the hard days behind us. He is enough. Cool it with water.
People fail; He doesn't. Ask for help. With hardship, ease.
On every one of those days, someone useful carried someone in: a driver at two in the morning, a friend with a card, a person with a pot of rice.

how: When someone dies, Muslim neighbors and friends bring meals to the bereaved family for several days, following the Prophet's instruction for Ja'far's family; service to anyone in need is counted as worship.

games.q: what does “the best of people” mean?
o: the people most useful to others, whoever the others are
the people who pray the most and fast the longest
the people born into the most respected families

games.q: the hard days, carried — tap the pairs.
p: said in the fire, said on the road

s: the hadith says the best are those most useful to Muslims
it says people: the best of people are those most useful to people.
when Ja'far died, the Prophet told people to make food for his family
food first: something had come upon them that kept them busy.
saying hasbunallah means pretending the danger isn't real
Ibrahim was really in the fire; the line says what's enough.

games.q: Jordan wants to help Khala Samina's family but worries: 'they're Muslim, i'm not. would that be weird?' what fits today?
o: the hadith says most useful to people; her help counts, and she's welcome.
it's kinder to let the masjid community handle it; it's their tradition.
she should wait until the family asks her, so she doesn't overstep.
games.why: people, both times, and the Qur'an's nations and tribes 'that ye may know one another'. a pot of rice needs no translation.

practice: Think of one person carrying something heavy right now. Skip the general offer; pick one specific, useful thing: a meal, a ride, a chore, an hour. Decide when you'll do it, and picture yourself at their door.

wordCard.voice: The best of people: those most useful to people. All people, the way the hadith says it.

orig.note: Arabic: the best of people are those most useful to people (al-Tabarani).

carryVoice: Your line: most useful. The best of people are often the ones who show up with the rice. Day done.

sources.ref: al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (the best of people are those most useful to people)
Sunan Abi Dawud 3132; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 998 (make food for the family of Ja'far)

sources.q: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct.
